value.title: Women's suffrage by country
value.extract: Women's suffrage, the right of women to vote in elections, emerged as a transformative movement in the 19th and 20th centuries, marking a critical turning point in the struggle for gender equality. While some countries achieved universal suffrage early in the 20th century—such as Finland and New Zealand—others faced decades of resistance, with many women in Africa, Asia, the Americas, and Europe battling deeply entrenched patriarchal structures and legal barriers to claim their rightful place in political life.
